premise: A deadpan retired mercenary hiding out in a filthy cyberpunk trailer park is forced back into action when his former partner—a terrifying assassin with an unnervingly calm presence—shows up seeking his help. The two have to survive a Yakuza kill squad while navigating the absurd, low-rent chaos of the trailer park and its aggressively trashy residents.
tone: Satirical, ridiculous, neon-grimy, and Adult Swim-style absurdist humor with a deadpan straight-man lead
setting: A super-trashy trailer park on the outskirts of a giant mega-city, where low-end cyberware, busted neon signage, junk tech, and bizarre locals collide with the looming presence of high-tech urban sprawl.
protagonist: A retired mercenary who was once one of the best in the business. Now living off the grid, he serves as a deadpan straight man: competent, dangerous, and profoundly out of place among the chaotic trailer park residents surrounding him.
core_hook: The protagonist’s former partner, now a terrifying assassin, comes to town and reveals that a Yakuza kill squad is hunting them both, forcing the ex-partners into an uneasy reunion and reluctant team-up.
must_have_elements: A super-trashy cyberpunk trailer park as the primary setting
A deadpan retired merc protagonist contrasted against ridiculous local residents
A former-partner rival dynamic between the protagonist and the assassin
A Yakuza kill squad as the main external threat
Strong emphasis on character comedy over pure action or mystery
Genre trope play and satire of cyberpunk conventions
Weird side characters and low-rent technology
Branching dialogue as the main player interaction
Light optional romance with the protagonist’s super-horny speed-freak neighbor
concept_summary: This Ren'Py visual novel is a satirical cyberpunk character comedy set in a trashy trailer park just outside a sprawling mega-city. The player follows a once-legendary retired mercenary, now trying to stay off the grid, whose deadpan professionalism is constantly undercut by the absurd residents around him. When his former partner—a chillingly calm assassin—arrives with news that a Yakuza kill squad is after them both, the story kicks into an uneasy buddy-crime survival spiral full of trope parody, low-rent future tech, and escalating neighborhood chaos. Optional branching dialogue can also steer a light romance with the protagonist’s wildly inappropriate speed-freak neighbor.
